solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Following wrong order like soldiers returned from leave? (4,2,5)

blocks.note: things in the wrong order run from the last to the first
soldiers whose leave is over go back to the front line

annotation.surface: Troops coming home from leave are marched off in the wrong order.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading as playful: the phrase taken literally, soldiers heading back to the front line.
annotation.definitionFit: Something done back to front follows the reverse of the proper order.

entries.clue: Bible incomplete? Voice criticism (3)

indicators.note: the word is left unfinished, losing its last letter

blocks.note: the Bible is the Good BOOK; drop its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone objects out loud to an edition of the Bible with pages missing.
annotation.walkthrough: The Bible is called 'the Book', so it stands for BOOK here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: jeering at a performer is the classic way to voice criticism.

entries.clue: Smoke starts off in garage filling vehicle (5)

indicators.note: take the first letters of the following words
the letters go inside, filling the next word

annotation.surface: Exhaust smoke builds up from a car left running in a garage.
annotation.walkthrough: C(IG)AR. 'Smoke' reads as fumes, but here it is a noun for something you smoke.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Smoke' as a noun is anything you smoke, as in 'fancy a smoke?', and a rolled tobacco leaf is one.

entries.clue: Queen once overwhelmed by strain hides here (7)

indicators.note: the queen is engulfed by the other word

blocks.note: to try is to strain, as in trying your patience
Queen Anne, a past British monarch

annotation.surface: A former queen, overcome by stress, goes into hiding.
annotation.walkthrough: T(ANNE)RY. 'Hides' looks like a verb, someone hiding; it is the noun, animal skins, which a tannery turns into leather.
annotation.definitionFit: A tannery is where hides are processed into leather.

entries.clue: In which one may grow the best cannabis? (9)

blocks.note: the flower of something is its finest part, as in 'the flower of youth'

annotation.surface: A grower asks where to raise top-quality cannabis.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one question about growing weed, but it splits: the definition is 'In which one may grow', and the wordplay is the best (flower) of cannabis (pot).
annotation.definitionFit: Description by function: a plant pot is the vessel in which things grow.

entries.clue: Concerning number of roach trails seen at intervals? (5)

indicators.note: only every other letter is visible

annotation.surface: A question about how many trails cockroaches leave, spotted here and there.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concerning number' looks like 'about how many'; it is the definition, as octal describes a number system (base eight).
annotation.definitionFit: Octal means relating to the base-eight number system.

entries.clue: Worker in ruse endlessly referencing Buddhist works (7)

indicators.note: the worker goes inside the ruse
the ruse loses its last letter

blocks.note: the ant is crosswords' standard worker

annotation.surface: An employee pulls a trick while citing Buddhist scriptures.
annotation.walkthrough: T(ANT)RIC. The tantras are sacred texts of some Hindu and Buddhist traditions.
annotation.definitionFit: Tantric means relating to the tantras, texts of Buddhist and Hindu practice.

entries.clue: I’m impressed by conference releasing prisoner (3)

indicators.note: the prisoner is let go, removed from the word

blocks.note: a powwow is a meeting or conference
POW = prisoner of war; taken away from POWWOW

annotation.surface: Someone is impressed that a peace conference has freed a prisoner.
annotation.walkthrough: POWWOW minus POW leaves WOW.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Wow!' is what you say when impressed.

entries.clue: Success keeps me bold, playing in tournament … (9)

indicators.note: the success holds the other letters inside
the letters are played with, rearranged

annotation.surface: A player says winning keeps them playing boldly in a tournament.
annotation.walkthrough: WI(MBLEDO)N. The ellipsis leads into the next clue, whose 'match' plays on the tennis theme.
annotation.definitionFit: Wimbledon is the tennis tournament held each summer in London.

entries.clue: … serving for the match? (7,4)

blocks.note: after a tennis clue this is the serve; here it is a portion of food
not a tennis match but a marriage, a good match

annotation.surface: Carrying on from the tennis clue: someone serving to win the match.
annotation.walkthrough: After 'tournament', 'serving for the match' is tennis talk; but a match is also a marriage, and a serving is a portion of food.
annotation.definitionFit: A wedding cake is what is served at a marriage celebration.

entries.clue: Church area unkempt for a long time (5,4)

indicators.note: untidy, so the letters are messed up

annotation.surface: Part of a church has been left untidy for ages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unkempt' sits between the definition and the fodder, so it looks like a description of the church area.
annotation.definitionFit: The organ loft is the gallery in a church where the organ stands.

entries.clue: Wanderer compos mentis in Glesga? (5)

blocks.note: compos mentis = sane, i.e. 'not mad'; the 'not' comes out as Glaswegian 'no'

annotation.surface: A drifter judged to be of sound mind in Glasgow.
annotation.walkthrough: Glesga is the local pronunciation of Glasgow, and Scots says 'no' for 'not', so 'not mad' becomes 'no mad'.
annotation.definitionFit: A nomad is someone who wanders with no fixed home.

entries.clue: Did you say pâté out of this world? Au contraire! (7)

definitions.text: out of this world? Au contraire!

indicators.note: points to how a word sounds when spoken

blocks.note: a terrine is a pâté-like dish

annotation.surface: A diner asks whether you called the pâté heavenly, then says quite the opposite.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is 'out of this world' turned round by 'au contraire': not unearthly but earthly. 'Out of this world' otherwise reads as praise for the pâté.
annotation.definitionFit: An inverted definition: the opposite of unearthly is earthly, which is the dictionary sense of the word.

entries.clue: Figure toned and rather developed (11)

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters; 'and' joins the two words

annotation.surface: Someone's physique is toned and fairly well developed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' reads as a body shape; it is a geometric figure.
annotation.definitionFit: A tetrahedron is a solid figure with four triangular faces.

entries.clue: Rock singer’s learning, ready for Romania (7)

blocks.note: ready = cash; the lei (plural of leu) is Romania's currency

annotation.surface: A rock musician is studying and has cash ready for a Romanian tour.
annotation.walkthrough: The Lorelei is a rock on the Rhine, and the siren said to sing there luring boatmen; not a rock star. 'Ready' as a noun means cash.
annotation.definitionFit: In legend the Lorelei is a siren singing from a rock on the Rhine.

entries.clue: Cheap adhesive (5)

blocks.note: cheap as in tasteless and shoddy-looking
adhesive as an adjective: slightly sticky, like drying paint

annotation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses of one word: tasteless, and sticky like drying paint.
annotation.definitionFit: Tacky means both cheap and nasty and slightly sticky.

entries.clue: Beaten about at noon, had little sleep (9)

indicators.note: the first word goes around the others

annotation.surface: Someone who was beaten up around midday got barely any sleep.
annotation.walkthrough: C(ATN)APPED. 'Beaten' is not the definition here; it means capped, surpassed.
annotation.definitionFit: To catnap is to take a short light sleep.

entries.clue: Alsatian? That’s poodle transformed with CGI! (6,3)

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A film has turned a poodle into an Alsatian using computer graphics.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is by example: an Alsatian (German shepherd) is a typical police dog, not the only kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Alsatians are the classic breed used as police dogs.

entries.clue: Listing omitting a great historic city (9)

indicators.note: leaves out the letter named

blocks.note: LEANING (listing, as a ship lists) without its A

annotation.surface: A catalogue leaves out a fine old city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Listing' reads as making a list; it is leaning over, as a ship does. Leningrad is the Soviet-era name of St Petersburg, hence historic.
annotation.definitionFit: Leningrad was the city's name from 1924 to 1991, so it is a city of history.

entries.clue: Uranium and fruit devoured by an android (9)

indicators.note: eaten, so taken inside the other word

blocks.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
a tomato is botanically a fruit

annotation.surface: A robot eats fruit and radioactive metal.
annotation.walkthrough: A(U TOMATO)N. 'An' does double duty in the surface as the article before 'android', but it is the container.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: an android is a machine built to act like a person, which is what a self-operating automaton is.

entries.clue: Violent wind and low cloud right by a lake (7)

blocks.note: mist is cloud at ground level

annotation.surface: A weather report: gales and low cloud near a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: The mistral is a strong cold wind that blows down the Rhône valley in southern France.
annotation.definitionFit: The mistral is a violent northerly wind of southern France.

entries.clue: Dance music on game shows (5)

indicators.note: the answer is on display inside the words

annotation.surface: A dance-music track played on a TV game show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dance music' looks like one phrase; 'Dance' alone is the definition and 'music' starts the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: The conga is a dance done in a single-file line.

entries.clue: Laugh from retired officer engaged in tiresome task (7)

indicators.note: gone back, so the letters run backwards
taken inside the other word

blocks.note: a chore is a tiresome task

annotation.surface: A retired officer busy with a dull job lets out a laugh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired officer' looks like a pensioner; 'retired' tells you to turn the officer round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Lewis Carroll's blend of chuckle and snort, for a gleeful laugh.

entries.clue: Passed by valley keeping especially to the west (7)

indicators.note: the valley holds the next part inside
in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

annotation.surface: Someone passed through a valley, keeping mostly to its western side.
annotation.walkthrough: D(ESP)ALE makes DESPALE, which read backwards gives ELAPSED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym used of time: hours that have gone by are said to have passed.

entries.clue: Duck unable to speak in Disney film? (5)

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

annotation.surface: A mute duck appearing in a Disney cartoon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' conjures Donald Duck, but it is a cricket duck, a score of zero, giving O.
annotation.definitionFit: Dumbo is Disney's 1941 film about a flying elephant.

entries.clue: Gaseous element consumed in recent delivery (7)

annotation.surface: A gas was used up in a recent shipment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' reads as a parcel; it is a birth, so a recent delivery is a newborn.
annotation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn baby, freshly delivered.

entries.clue: Female dismissed by more attractive maiden? (5)

indicators.note: the female is sent away from the word

annotation.surface: A young woman is dropped in favour of a prettier maiden.
annotation.walkthrough: A maiden is an old British word for a clothes horse, a frame for drying laundry; the question mark marks the unexpected sense.
annotation.definitionFit: An airer, like a maiden, is a frame for drying clothes.

entries.clue: More mature one training at school between runs (5)

indicators.note: the letters sit between two others

blocks.note: r = run, twice for 'runs'; the outside

annotation.surface: An older pupil doing PE between runs.
annotation.walkthrough: R(I PE)R. Runs gives two Rs, one each side.
annotation.definitionFit: Riper means more mature, like fruit.

entries.clue: Delays speaker aboard westbound train (9)

indicators.note: on board, so inside the other word
in an across clue, heading west means read right to left

blocks.note: to train a gun on something is to aim it
an orator is a public speaker

annotation.surface: Hold-ups as an announcer boards a westbound train.
annotation.walkthrough: M(ORATOR)IA. 'Train' looks like the railway, but it is the verb, to aim.
annotation.definitionFit: Moratoria (plural of moratorium) are temporary suspensions or delays.

entries.clue: Sack poor writers in Bow for speaking out (3)

indicators.note: says the answer comes from a spoken sound

blocks.note: hacks are poor writers; Bow is in London's East End, where Cockneys drop the H

annotation.surface: Firing bad journalists in Bow for voicing opinions.
annotation.walkthrough: Hacks are low-grade journalists. Bow is a district of east London, and Cockney speech drops initial H, so hacks there sound like 'acks'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from workplace slang: to dismiss an employee is to give them the chop.

entries.clue: Make careless error, with which mood becomes low? (3)

blocks.note: a lapse of attention, as when a tired person drifts off for a moment
split the answer in two: take away the letter D and MOOD becomes MOO, a cow's low

annotation.surface: A slip that sends someone's spirits down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low' reads as gloomy, but it is a cow's moo. The saying 'Homer nods' means even the best make careless mistakes.
annotation.definitionFit: To nod is to make a lapse through inattention, as in 'even Homer nods'.

entries.clue: Go-go dancing with elderly politician in the past (5,6)

indicators.note: dancers never keep still, and letters that are dancing swap places until they land in a new order

annotation.surface: An old statesman once took to go-go dancing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Elderly politician' looks like the definition, but 'elderly' is fodder; David Lloyd George was British Prime Minister from 1916 to 1922.
annotation.definitionFit: Lloyd George is a politician of the past, a Liberal Prime Minister.
